turns.answer:
Because I made two unsupported assumptions. I treated your description as establishing Article 11 coverage, and I treated Section 11-134(a) as the rule that automatically calculates your pension.

The Code shows that Section 11-134(a) is a **minimum-annuity** provision. It can apply to certain employees who withdraw with at least 20 years of service, but it contains several different formulas, elections, reductions, and exceptions. It is not a general statement that every Article 11 pension is calculated under that subsection. [40 ILCS 5/11-134]

Your record places you in Article 11, but your statement that you are a park employee does not itself establish that coverage. The Code sections read here explain how service is counted for minimum-annuity and other annuity purposes; they do not establish from the job title alone which Article covers you. [40 ILCS 5/11-215] [40 ILCS 5/11-216]

So the wording “as a park employee covered by Article 11” was inaccurate. I should have said that your record places you in Article 11, and that the applicable pension provision would depend on the circumstances of your withdrawal and the particular annuity you elect or qualify for. turns.question: What does Section 11-134 say about the annuity formula?
turns.answer:
Section 11-134 provides several annuity formulas. For an employee who withdraws on or after January 1, 2002, with at least 20 years of service, one formula is **2.40% of the highest average annual salary for any 4 consecutive years within the last 10 years of service for each year of service**. The maximum is generally **80% of that salary measure**. [40 ILCS 5/11-134]

The section also provides an alternative formula of **2.40% for each year of service**, based on the same 4-year salary average. That is an election between formulas, not a separate automatic benefit. Section 11-134 also includes formulas using 1.67%, 1.90%, 2.10%, 2.30%, 1.80%, 2.00%, 2.20%, and 2.40%, depending on the withdrawal date and other eligibility conditions. [40 ILCS 5/11-134]

For minimum-annuity purposes, service is counted under Section 11-216. Six or more months in a year count as one year, while at least one month but less than six months counts as one-half year. [40 ILCS 5/11-216]

The statute also allows an annuity that begins before age 60 to be reduced by **0.25% for each full month or fractional part of a month** before age 60, unless a listed age-and-service exception applies. Section 11-134 does not provide enough information here to determine which formula or exception would produce your benefit amount. The salary used for the calculation and your intended withdrawal and annuity-start dates are needed. The statute also refers to Section 11-221 and Section 11-164, which were not available here, so I could not establish any conclusion that depends on those provisions.
